item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 020522
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Thu Oct 1 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Nolo, located several hundred miles west-northwest of Lihue,
Hawaii, and on Hurricane Rachel, located a couple of hundred miles
south of the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

South of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form late this weekend or
early next week south of the southern coast of Mexico. Thereafter,
environmental conditions appear favorable for gradual development,
and a tropical depression is likely to form by the middle of next
week while the system moves slowly west-northwestward to
northwestward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

$$
Forecaster Evans/Gibbs

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Public Advisory Number 20
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Thu Oct 01 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 020233
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Rachel Advisory Number  20
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 PM MST Thu Oct 01 2026
 
...RACHEL HOLDING STEADY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM MST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.5N 109.9W
ABOUT 235 MI...380 KM S OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...120 MPH...195 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 290 DEGREES AT 3 MPH...6 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...950 MB...28.06 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM MST (0300 UTC), the center of Hurricane Rachel was located 
near latitude 19.5 North, longitude 109.9 West. Rachel is moving 
toward the west-northwest near 3 mph (6 km/h), and this slow 
westward to west-northwestward motion is expected during the next 
couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 120 mph (195 km/h) with higher
gusts. Rachel is a category 3 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson 
Hurricane Wind Scale. Additional strengthening is forecast within 
the next 24 h, followed by gradual weakening this weekend.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 150 miles
(240 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 950 mb (28.06 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Rachel will affect the coast of 
west-central Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula through the 
weekend. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and 
rip current conditions. Please consult products from your local 
weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Gibbs

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 20
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Thu Oct 01 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 020235
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Rachel Discussion Number  20
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 PM MST Thu Oct 01 2026
 
Satellite imagery indicates that the convective structure associated
with Rachel has changed little over the past several hours. A ragged
eye surrounded by deep convection with cloud-top temperatures as
cold as -85 C persists, although the coverage of the coldest cloud
tops has decreased slightly. The subjective Dvorak intensity
estimate from TAFB is T5.5/102 kt, which aligns with the latest
objective estimates. Given these estimates and the relatively steady
satellite presentation, the initial intensity is held at 105 kt.
 
The initial motion is west-northwestward, or 290/3 kt. Little change 
in motion is expected during the next day or so while the system 
remains within a weak steering environment. Thereafter, a mid-level 
ridge is forecast to build to the north, supporting a more westward 
track with the forward speed gradually increasing through the 
remainder of the forecast period. A gradual bend toward the 
west-northwest is forecast between 96 and 120 h as the ridge begins 
to weaken. The track guidance remains in generally good agreement on 
this scenario, although some differences remain in the timing of the 
acceleration. The latest NHC track forecast is similar to the 
previous prediction and lies near the HCCA and GDMI aids.
 
Environmental conditions should remain largely favorable for some 
additional strengthening during the next 24 h. Some 
east-northeasterly vertical wind shear may continue to affect the 
cyclone during this time, although Rachel's well-established 
inner-core structure should allow for additional strengthening in 
the short term. Thereafter, increasingly dry mid-level air is 
forecast to begin wrapping into the system, while some 
east-northeasterly shear could persist. These factors should 
gradually disrupt the inner-core structure and induce a weakening 
trend. Increasingly marginal sea surface temperatures later in the 
forecast period should support continued weakening through day 5. 
The latest NHC intensity forecast is essentially unchanged from the 
previous advisory, showing Rachel reaching a peak intensity of 115 
kt within the next 12 h. This peak remains above the intensity 
guidance, with the forecast thereafter gradually trending toward the 
upper end of the guidance envelope.
